summary: Shasta County ground-type lookout site on North Fork Mountain: FFLA lists it gone and peakbagging an LO site at 5,358 ft; the only dated item (1923) does not name this mountain.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists it gone; peakbagging labels the site an LO site (building removed); no source describes what remains

corrections.why: Checked against the peak table row for North Fork Mtn (LO site): Shasta-Trinity is in the Forest column (cite 3). facts.agency already reads Shasta-Trinity National Forest.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The only dated item on Kemnow's page is a 1923 clipping about a lookout station at the head of Squaw Creek. It does not name North Fork Mountain, so it is not attributed to this site and the story says so.

sources.title: North Fork Mountain, Forest Lookouts (Ron Kemnow)

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Kemnow's page has one dated item, a 1923 Blue Lake Advocate clipping about a lookout station at the head of Squaw Creek, a tributary of the Pit River. It does not name North Fork Mountain, so it is not used as build or staffing history. FFLA: Ground type, Gone, no register number. Peakbagging: LO site, elevation 5,358 ft; the Shasta-Trinity forest value was checked against the table's Forest column on 2026-10-10. Do not confuse with the West Virginia North Fork Mountain (Pendleton County, Smoke Hole); a Wikipedia article under that name was read and is about the wrong mountain. No staffing, fire or removal record found. Two WebSearch calls returned nothing usable for this site.
